overview: Marshallese communities connect island life with canoe skills and knowledge of the sea. Contemporary training carries craft traditions into new livelihoods and forms of exchange.

items.text: Marshallese stick charts represent relationships among ocean swells and islands. They should not be described as maps of currents.
Charts combine slender framework elements with shells or junctions marking islands. They were generally teaching aids ashore rather than charts carried aboard.
Mattang charts teach abstract wave relationships; meddo and rebbelib show relative island arrangements at different regional scales. Individual charts vary.
Waan Aelon in Majel trains young people through canoe building and related skills. School visits also introduce students to the work.
Instructors and trainees make model canoes, coconut graters and stick charts. Income from their work is reinvested in the programme.
The Compact of Free Association with the United States entered into force on 21 October 1986. This modern state relationship did not begin Marshallese cultural history.
